سَمِيقٌ : see سَامِقٌ. ＝
-A2- The dual, سَمِيقَانِ, signifies The [yokes or] two pieces of wood that belong to the نِير, surrounding the necks of the two bulls, (S, Z, O, K,) like the neck-ring, (S, O,) the two extremities of each being made to meet together beneath the bull's dewlap, and bound with a cord: (Z, TA:) pl. أَسْمِقَةٌ. (TA.) ―
-b2- And [its pl.,] أَسْمِقَةٌ, Certain pieces of wood in the utensil upon which bricks, or crude bricks, (لَبِن,) are conveyed. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, L, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
